Memory updated and the skill reference patched.

Summary of what I saved (this question passed, but it exposed a real, generalizable discriminator worth capturing):

The key insight: the exact phrasing of the defense question determines which column to use, and the two phrasings point OPPOSITE directions —

- "national defense" alone (WWII 1941-43 ratio questions) → the NARROW National Defense classification row, NOT War Activities. (Prior failure: 0.4804 wrong, gold 0.6841.)
- "national defense AND associated activities" → the BROADER consolidated aggregate, not the narrow row. (This question: 1953 vs 1940, summing all 12 monthly cells per year, abs %chg = 1608.80% — CORRECT.)

Also noted the era effect: by the 1950s the "War activities" classification is gone (post-WWII), so that specific trap doesn't apply to 1950s bulletins.

I updated both:
- The memory note (replaced the old WWII-only warning so a future run won't wrongly pick the narrow row when the question says "and associated activities").
- The references/calendar-year-from-monthly.md file in the officeqa-treasury-bulletin skill, with a "PHRASING DISCRIMINATOR" section, the working method, and an era note.

The method itself (sum all individual monthly cells for each calendar year, then (later−earlier)/earlier×100, absolute value, round to the clause's decimal places) was already consistent with existing guidance, so no new procedure was needed there.
